verdict.reasoning: Doctor opens with “you are feeling hot and have had severe headaches” and patient confirms; patient also reports “some tingling in my arms.”
Patient says headaches are “really affecting my work” and occur “generally during work times… I get it mostly when I’m at work… I’m in a meeting or in my laptop.”
When asked location, patient says “No, it’s mostly in the front, and then, yeah, it kind of stays there,” indicating no radiation/migration.
Patient states “I kind of feel a little bit nauseous, maybe” when describing the headaches.
Doctor asks “So do you feel short of breath while you’re sitting at your desk?” and patient answers “Yeah. No. Yes. Sorry. Yeah,” confirming shortness of breath at the desk.
Patient reports tingling “in my arms” and clarifies it is in “Both” hands and describes it as “Prickling? Yeah.” (arms/hands as tingling sites).
Regarding heart beating fast, when asked frequency, patient says “it’s maybe once a day, maybe more,” consistent with about once per day.
Patient says “I do have, like, some loss of libido at home” and when asked duration: “Same amount of time. Really? Like, since I changed my job.”
Reduced appetite: “I kind of lose my appetite also.” Weight loss: “Have you lost weight?” – “Yes.” “Can you remember how much?” – “5Lbs.” “It’s not intentional. No.”
Patient states “Well, I have a hypothyroidism.”
When asked about medication, patient says “Thyroxine.”
Doctor asks “are you allergic to anything?” and patient replies “No.”
Patient answers occupation: “I’m a lawyer.” Stress: doctor asks for 1–10 scale and patient responds “I think it’s seven or eight… it’s like a law firm. Like, there’s always pressure.”

Alcohol: “Like once a week. A couple of glasses.” Smoking: “And how about smoking?” – “No.” Drugs: “do you do anything else recreational in terms of drugs?” – “No… never taken cocaine or marijuana?” – “No.”

No exam is performed in the call; doctor says “I think the best course of action is you come and see one of our doctors in the clinic. We can give you an examination,” implying it is deferred to the in‑person visit.
Transcript notes headaches occur mostly at work and patient has high stress, but the doctor never explicitly assesses or states that headaches are associated with work stress.
Palpitations and tingling are described, but the doctor never mentions anxiety or considers it explicitly in the discussion.

Hypothyroidism is discussed and medication adherence confirmed: “Well, I have a hypothyroidism.” “Do you take medications for that?” – “Thyroxine.” “And are you remembering to take your medications?” – “Yes.” Doctor also plans “blood tests for your thyroxin.”
Unintentional weight loss and loss of libido are reported and temporally associated with job change, but no explicit statement links them causally to stress in the transcript.
Doctor says “I think the best course of action is you come and see one of our doctors in the clinic… I’m going to do is book an appointment, or I think you can book an appointment through the app.”

Doctor plans in‑person exam: “We can give you an examination. And what that means is we check your heart and your breathing, make sure that those things are functioning correctly,” which implies a physical exam and vitals/heart–lung assessment.
Doctor states “and probably do some blood tests for your thyroxin.” This implies thyroid function blood tests are planned.
Stress is discussed, but there is no stated plan to discuss stress management strategies in the future visit.
